comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose revenue changes driven by specific product categories within their semiconductor segments, though the direction and drivers differ significantly. AMD reports a substantial 58% decrease in its Gaming segment net revenue ($2.6 billion) specifically attributed to lower semi-custom product revenue. In contrast, Broadcom's Semiconductor Solutions segment net revenue increased, driven by strong demand for AI networking products, although this was partially offset by lower demand in other areas like broadband and server storage. Both disclosures break down revenue performance by distinct product lines (semi-custom vs. AI networking/broadband) to explain the financial results.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center and AI (DCAI) Revenue and Volume Analysis
comparisons.peer_summary: DCAI revenue decreased $4.2 billion from 2022, driven by lower server demand; server volume decreased 37% due to a softening CPU data center market, while server ASPs increased 20% due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer revenue and a higher mix of high core count products.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel attribute significant revenue declines to softer demand in their respective core hardware segments, highlighting a broader market weakness in specific CPU/AI server and gaming markets. AMD's Gaming segment revenue fell 58% due to lower semi-custom product revenue. Similarly, Intel's Data Center and AI (DCAI) segment revenue decreased, driven by lower server demand and a 37% drop in server volume due to a 'softening CPU data center market.' While AMD's decline is specific to the Gaming semi-custom products and Intel's is in the general CPU server volume, both disclosures cite reduced demand/volume in their respective processor-centric segments as a primary negative driver.

sentences.text: The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue.

comparisons.peer_summary: Total revenue for 2023 decreased 49% compared to 2022, primarily due to a 51% drop in DRAM sales (high-40% ASP decline and high-single-digit shipment decline) and a 46% drop in NAND sales (low-50% ASP decline partially offset by high-single-digit shipment increases).
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze revenue performance by decomposing it into volume/shipment changes and Average Selling Price (ASP) impacts, a common method for semiconductor memory and logic companies. AMD attributes its Gaming revenue decline to 'lower semi-custom product revenue,' which implies a combination of shipment and/or ASP changes. Micron provides a more explicit decomposition in its total revenue decline analysis, separating the impact of ASP declines (e.g., high-40% range for DRAM) from bit shipment declines (high-single-digit range). While AMD does not explicitly break down the 'lower revenue' into ASP vs. Volume in the provided sentence, the analytical framework of decomposing revenue changes into these two components is present in both, though Micron's data is more granular regarding the specific percentages of ASP vs. Volume contribution.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fiscal 2024 gross margin performance and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023, primarily driven by 217% growth in Data Center revenue and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA discuss the impact of revenue mix and product performance on their financial results, but in opposite directions. AMD's Gaming segment revenue declined 58% due to lower semi-custom product revenue. NVIDIA, conversely, saw its overall gross margin increase driven by a 217% growth in Data Center revenue, which represents a strong shift towards high-growth AI products. While AMD's disclosed segment is contracting, NVIDIA's disclosed segment (Data Center) is expanding rapidly, illustrating the divergent performance between traditional gaming/semi-custom markets and the booming AI infrastructure market in the same fiscal period.
